about: The block product's declared actions, run by the generic executor (package declared). Each action names where it runs, its parameters, what its invocation records, one or more variants (the first whose condition holds runs), each with its command as a template, a timeout, a decoding of the answer and the citation of the product's command and flags, read at read_at. Every substituted value is one shell-quoted word. Outcomes of error bodies come from outcomes.json, by (decode.action or the verb, decode.path, code). Templates name config.<key> (the shared configuration below), a parameter, <subject param>.<field> (a volume: name, nqn, layout_id, epoch, pid, pid_start, written; the current host's server, data_addr, ctrl_addr, status_addr, nvme_addr; the move target's next_cur, next_server, next_data_addr, next_ctrl_addr; holder_alive: the recorded holder runs. A process: pid, pid_start, killed_pid, killed_argv, volume, and its volume's fields), variant, and in a decoding answer.<field>, stderr or exit. Every action has a runner deadline: the RUNNER's bound on one operation, never a product bound and never a checker's. A declared command runs detached on its node (its output and exit code in files under runner_io_dir, polled), so nothing can hold the runner past the deadline; at it the command's session is killed, the operation completes unknown with the detail 'timeout after <n>s', and any process that survives the kill is recorded under 'abandoned' by pid and start time. A declared deadline lies above the command's own bound, so it ends only a call that does not answer. An exception's deadline grows by its plus_param's seconds (a wait the step may set). The step kinds (package declared) run one operation under the action's own runner_deadline_seconds: device (I/O through the subject's block device), process (a long-lived process by its recorded identity: start, kill, restart) and sequence (product steps that feed each other; any failure after the first state change is unknown). The exceptions are the actions that stay Go handlers, each with its reason.

runner_setup.why: writes the cluster spec file the blockmaster reads and the runner's own record of each volume (hosts, ports, NQN); it calls no product command or API and records nothing in the history
computes one run's ports, work directory and NQN prefix from port_base and the run's tag and sets them as vars; no command runs and nothing is recorded

exceptions.why: a fault's repair whose blockmaster case is not declared: the blockmaster relaunches through the ownership script's spawn, which records the new identity in the ledger, the identity is read back from the ledger whatever spawn's exit, it is ready when a master call (a resolve of the first volume) answers ok or refused, and after it the unit's supervision relaunches holders that fenced while the master was down. A holder's restart is declared (v3_op_restart_holder): this handler hands every other process to it, unchanged
exceptions.declarable_with: a process restart whose launcher is a declared command that records the identity itself (read back from a ledger subject), a readiness probe that is a self-reported answer of ok or refused, and a step after the operation that runs the unit's supervision

exceptions.why: an observation of health after faults: polls the master and every live holder within a bound
exceptions.declarable_with: an observation over every subject of a kind (the master and each live holder) polled until a declared health condition holds within a bound

guest.about: Runner settings for the guest, the kernel NVMe/TCP host the runner connects to a volume. They are not product facts and never checker bounds. A run names its connect with the run var connect.select_var; absent, it is the default. The runner's own bound on one read, write or flush through the kernel block device is each device action's io.runner_deadline_seconds: under the product's plain connect the kernel keeps I/O to a dead controller blocked for ctrl_loss_tmo (600 s by default), so the runner runs the I/O detached, ends the operation as unknown at that deadline and records the abandoned child by pid and start time.

connect.about: A variant is DECLARED here, named, with its source and evidence false; a run selects one by name with the run var select_var (a scenario env value), and empty selects the default. Its options go into the kernel's fabrics connect string under the kernel's option names, in the order of options (the runner connects through /dev/nvme-fabrics, not nvme-cli, whose flags are --ctrl-loss-tmo, --reconnect-delay, --fast_io_fail_tmo, --keep-alive-tmo). A variant's option names may be written with _ or -; an unknown name, a value that is not an integer, or a name given twice refuses the description at load. A variant is named 'guest connect variant: <values>' in the run header and in every attach, is never release evidence, and no checker changes with it.
